initial_requirements: Users need a video-search application that can query multiple websites at once for streaming sources and downloadable video listings. A user should be able to search for a specific title or genre, choose which types of sources to include, compare organized results, and retain useful favorites. System maintainers also need a way to control which external sites participate in searches.

turns.interviewer_utterance:
Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about your video-search project so we can understand the requirements clearly and avoid missing anything important.

Before we begin, are you aligned with the scope of this interview, or do your expectations differ?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, I’m aligned with that scope. We want to clarify how the video search should work across multiple sites, what users need to do with the results, and what controls maintainers need over the sources.

turns.interviewer_utterance: To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I’m part of the team sponsoring the x-ray Video Search project, and I’m helping define what the application needs to do from a business and user perspective. I’m here to make sure we capture the practical workflow for searching, filtering, and managing external video sources.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you describe the current process or system you use today for searching across video sources and managing any favorites or source controls?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Right now it’s pretty fragmented. People search one site at a time, keep their own notes or bookmarks for favorites, and there isn’t a central place to compare results or control which sources are included. For maintainers, source selection is mostly manual and handled outside of any unified tool.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what features do you hope to get from this project?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We want to replace the one-site-at-a-time workflow with a single search that can query multiple approved sources together. We also want results to be easier to compare, and for users to save favorites in the app instead of relying on browser bookmarks or notes. On the admin side, we need a straightforward way to enable or disable external sites without touching code.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Based on your description, do you think support for filtering search sources by streaming versus downloadable content should also be included?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that should be included. Users should be able to choose whether they want streaming sources, downloadable listings, or both, because that’s part of how they’ll narrow down the search in practice.

turns.interviewer_utterance: So these are the features/functions you want to have: multi-site search across approved sources, result comparison, in-app favorites, admin enable/disable source control, and filtering by streaming versus downloadable sources, right?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that matches what we need. Those are the core functions we’re expecting for the initial version.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which of those core functions should be the highest priority for the initial version?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The highest priority should be the multi-site search across approved sources, along with the ability to filter by streaming versus downloadable content. Those are the main user-facing capabilities we need working first, because without them the product doesn’t really deliver its core value.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want the multi-site search to accomplish.
turns.interviewee_utterance: It should let a user enter a title or genre once and get results from several approved sites at the same time. The results should come back in a consistent format so people can compare them without jumping between sites, and ideally they should see which source each result came from. If possible, it should also handle basic relevance sorting so the best matches appear first.

turns.interviewer_utterance: How should the search behave when a source is unavailable or returns no results for a query?
turns.interviewee_utterance: If a source is down or times out, the search should still return whatever results it can from the other sources and clearly indicate that one source failed. If a source simply has no matches, that should be shown as no results for that source rather than an error. The user shouldn’t lose the whole search just because one site has an issue.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want the source filtering to accomplish.
turns.interviewee_utterance: The filtering should let users limit searches to only streaming sources, only downloadable listings, or both. That way they can avoid irrelevant results and focus on the type of content they actually want. It should apply before or during the search so the results come back already narrowed down, not just filtered after the fact.

turns.interviewer_utterance: How should users choose between streaming sources, downloadable listings, or both in the interface?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I’d expect simple toggles or checkboxes near the search box, so it’s obvious and quick to change before running a search. It should default to both unless the user selects otherwise, because that’s the broadest search.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What level of detail should be shown for each search result so users can compare them effectively?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Each result should show the title, the source site, and whether it’s streaming or downloadable. If available, I’d also want a short description and maybe a quality or size indicator, since that helps people judge whether a result is worth opening. It doesn’t need to be exhaustive, just enough to compare options at a glance.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Favorites are important, because users will likely want to save good sources or searches and come back to them later. I’d also want maintainers to have an admin control area where they can add, remove, or disable external sites without redeploying the whole app. Beyond that, maybe basic search history would be useful, but I’d treat that as secondary.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which of those should be the highest priority next: favorites, admin source control, or search history?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Admin source control should be the highest priority, because the whole system depends on which sites are allowed into the search. Favorites would be next since that directly helps users keep useful results. Search history would be nice to have, but it feels less essential than the other two.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want the admin source control to accomplish.
turns.interviewee_utterance: It should let maintainers decide which external sites are included in searches and switch them on or off without changing code. They should be able to block a source temporarily if it becomes unreliable or problematic, and bring it back later if needed. Ideally it would also show whether a source is currently active and maybe when it was last checked, so admins can manage the list confidently.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you describe who should be able to access the admin source control area and how those permissions should work?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Only authorized maintainers should be able to access it, not regular users. I’d expect a small set of admin accounts with permission to view and change the source list, while regular users can only search and save favorites. If there are different maintainer roles, I’d be open to separating read-only access from full edit access, but that’s something I’d want to confirm with the team.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want the favorites feature to accomplish.
turns.interviewee_utterance: Favorites should let users save individual results or sources they find useful, so they can get back to them later without searching again. I’d want them to be able to view a favorites list, remove items, and probably organize them a bit if possible, but the core need is just quick retrieval. If it’s easy to do, saving the search criteria too would be helpful, though I’m not sure that’s required.
